summary: Wei Lin specializes in sinology and history/archaeology. Lin studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and under John C. Huntington at Ohio State University (PhD attested 2007). Posts include Transylvania University, University of Michigan, Western Michigan University, and Nanjing Municipal Museum.
Wei Wu is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the International Buddhist College. Attested in 2026, Wu serves as Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University.

Wei-Cheng Lin works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. Lin served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015 and joined the University of Chicago faculty in 2015.

Wei-jen Teng works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Teng studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University (PhD attested 2011, supervised by Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil), and served at Chung-Hwa Institute and DILA.

Wei-ming Tu is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Tunghai University and Harvard (PhD 1968). He held posts at Princeton (1968–1971), UC Berkeley (1971–1981), Harvard (1999–2010), and directed the Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008).

Weijue Shi was a Buddhist studies figure who was ordained under Linyuan in 1963 and studied under Lingshuan. Shi founded the Chung Tai Shan order, Lin Quan Temple in 1987, and Chung Tai Buddhist Institute in 1993.

Weiqiang Wang specializes in linguistics, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. Wang earned a PhD from Guangdong University of Foreign Studies (2009–2013), taught there starting in 2005, and held a research post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012).
Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Shen held teaching posts at the University of Hong Kong and at Renmin University of China (~2006–2020).
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Weizhong Huang works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Huang held a post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and serves as a professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

Weldon South Coblin is a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology who studied under Fang-Kuei Li (~1967–1972). He served as Professor at the University of Iowa (~1973–2014), where he became Professor Emeritus of Chinese in ~2014.
Wen-ling Jane is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jane earned a PhD at Columbia University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and teacher Lozang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai works in Indology and linguistics. Mai studied at the University of Hamburg, Kyoto University, and Peking University (PhD), and served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Stanford University (-1998) and has held positions at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (attested 2018–2026).

Wendy Doniger specializes in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She earned PhDs from Harvard (1968, under Daniel H. H. Ingalls) and Oxford (1973, under Robert Charles Zaehner), and joined the University of Chicago faculty in 1978.
Wenjiang Ding was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Peking University and was a student of Qichao Liang (~1918–1929). Ding held a post at Peking University from ~1913 to 1920.

Wenjie Duan worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and Central Academy of Fine Arts, and spent his career at Dunhuang Academy, serving as Acting Head, First Deputy Director, Director, and honorary director.
Wenjie Qin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu.
Wenzhuo Shi is a researcher in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, studying as a PhD student and researcher at Ghent University (attested 2022 and 2026).

Werner Abraham was a linguist who studied at TU Wien, University of Innsbruck, and University of Vienna (PhD ~1965). He held posts at Illinois, Tübingen, and an ordinary professorship in German linguistics and medieval studies at Groningen from 1971.
